input.quote: Array shall not require Ono to place orders directly with a Subcontractor if such Subcontractor is unwilling to fulfill such orders on terms as favorable to Ono as the terms such Subcontractors have extended to Array.
input.rationale: We searched the payment, royalty, covenant and manufacturing/supply provisions (Articles VI, VII, VIII and IX) and the definitions for MFN-style language ("most favored", "(no less/more) favorable", "best price", matching third-party terms). There is no obligation on Ono to extend to Array any better terms granted to a third party or to match third-party offers, so the agreement sits at our preferred position (no MFN burden on the customer). The only comparable-terms language, Section 9.x(b), runs in our favour by requiring that Subcontractor orders placed by Ono be on terms as favourable to Ono as those extended to Array; consistent with the rule, we leave that vendor-side benefit untouched. Article 8.2's exclusivity covenant is a non-compete, not an MFN, and is addressed under other rules if at all.
